titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§182–185: Baljuna, Arqal-Kögi and the Jeje'er Height
part: §§182–185 — Baljuna, Arqal-Kögi and the Jeje'er Height
about: Four sections of flight and return. In §182 Chinggis camps at Lake Baljuna and meets a trader and the Qorulas; in §183 Qasar, who had left his family with Wang Qan, finds his brother again and sends two men to Wang Qan with a message of his own, setting a meeting place at Arqal-Kögi. §184 is the envoys' reception: Wang Qan, feasting in his golden tent, sends the trusted Itürgen back with them, who sees something at the meeting place and bolts, and is shot, caught and killed. In §185 the envoys report Wang Qan unguarded, Chinggis surrounds him at Jeje'er Height for three days and nights, the Kereid give in, and Qadaq-Ba'atur, who covered Wang Qan's escape, is spared and the Quildar favours are decreed. The grammar is converb chains ending in one finite verb, speeches nested in speeches (the colons and quotation marks in the print help), reflexive-possessives that follow the speaker, and the optative -tügei in the decrees. Several lines are hard, and the notes say where. The Mongol readings follow Shiratori; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Tedüi Čiṅgis Qaγan oduγ̇ad Balžuna naγ̇ur baγ̇uba.
sentences.l: Thereupon Čiṅgis Qaγan, having gone, lake Balžuna descended.
sentences.i: Then Chinggis Qahan went on and made camp at Lake Baljuna.
sentences.n: Tedüi (Ming 卽便) is a sentence adverb, 'thereupon', that opens a new step; oduγ̇ad is od- 'go' + the converb -γad, 'having gone'. baγ̇u- is 'descend' (Ming 下), here 'light down, halt, camp'. Balžuna naγ̇ur takes no case ending: it is simply the place he came down at. Naγ̇ur is 'lake' (Ming 海子, 'sea-child').

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Baljuna, a lake or water (place name) [海︀子名]
to descend, come down, halt [下了]

sentences.t: Tende baγ̇uqui-dur Soγ̇os-Čaγan Qorulas žöb tende učirlalduba.
sentences.l: There, at the descending, Soγ̇os-Čaγan Qorulas, žöb, there meeting-one-another.
sentences.i: While he was camped there, he met Soqos-Chaqan of the Qorulas.
sentences.n: baγ̇uqui-dur is the pattern to learn: a participle in -qui + the dative-locative -dur, 'at the camping', i.e. 'when, while' (the Ming gives 下的 時, 'at the time of descending'). učirlalduba has the reciprocal -ldu-, 'meet one another' (Ming 相遇着了). The word žöb (Ming 是) sits oddly between the name and the second tende; I take it as an emphasis ('just there'), but that is a guess.

morph.gloss: there, then (locative adverb from tere) [那裏]
right, proper; here perhaps "exactly, just" or an emphatic particle (uncertain) [是]
there, then (locative adverb from tere) [那裏]
to meet, come upon (stem inferred) [相遇着了]

sentences.t: Tede Qorulas ülü bulγan elsen irebe.
sentences.l: Those Qorulas not fighting, submitting, came.
sentences.i: Those Qorulas came in submission, without a fight.
sentences.n: A converb chain: bulγan 'fighting' and elsen 'submitting' hang on the one finite verb irebe 'came'. ülü 'not' negates the converb bulγan (Ming 不 鬭). Both stems are inferred from the Ming glosses (鬭 'fight', 投降 'surrender'), not from a form I can check.

morph.gloss: to fight, strive (stem from the Ming 鬭) [鬭]
to submit (stem inferred from the Ming 投降) [投降]

sentences.t: Öṅgüd-ü Alaqu-Šidigid-Quri-dāča Asan Sartaγtai čaγan temeġetü miṅγan irges daγ̇užu
sentences.l: Öṅgüd's Alaqu-Šidigid-Quri-from Asan, Sartaγtai, white camel-having, a thousand wethers driving,
sentences.i: Asan, a Sartaqtai, who came from Alaqush-Digit-Quri of the Ongut, was driving a thousand wethers and had white camels,
sentences.n: The Ming says only 'tribe' for Sartaγtai and 'person' for Asan. I take Sartaγ to be the Mongol word for the Muslim merchants of Central Asia, but that is my background knowledge, not the gloss. -dāča is the ablative -ača after the dative -da, with the Ming 處 'at the place of': Asan comes from Alaqu-Šidigid-Quri's people. temeġetü is temeġe 'camel' + the possessive -tü, 'camel-having'. The sentence is left open; its verb comes two units on.

morph.gloss: ablative: from (long-vowel form, after the dative -da)
a man of the Sartaγ (Ming 種名); Sartaγ + -tai, person of (analysis uncertain) [種(名)]
wether sheep, castrated ram (Ming 羯羊) [羯羊]
to drive along (stem inferred from the Ming 趕; uncertain) [趕着]

sentences.t: Ergüne müren huruγ̇u buluγad keremüd qudaldužu abura aisurun Balžuna usulan oroqui-dur učiraba.
sentences.l: Ergüne river along, sables, squirrels, trading, in-order-to-take, when coming, Balžuna water drinking, at the entering, met.
sentences.i: He had come down the Ergüne River to trade for sable and squirrel pelts, and as he came, entering the Baljuna to drink its water, he met them.
sentences.n: A converb chain again, with a purpose converb (abura 'in order to take'), a time converb (aisurun 'when coming') and the participle clause oroqui-dur 'at the entering'; the finite verb is last (učiraba 'met'). The verb has no stated object or subject, and I have supplied 'he' and 'them': it is Asan who meets Chinggis's people, but the Mongol does not say so. buluγad and keremüd are plurals in -d (Ming 貂鼠每, 靑鼠每). usulan 'drinking' is read from the Ming 飮; I take usu 'water' + -la-.

morph.gloss: squirrel (Ming 靑鼠 grey squirrel; form uncertain) [靑鼠每]
to trade, buy and sell (stem inferred from the Ming 買) [買着]
converb of purpose: in order to
Baljuna, a lake or water (place name) [水名]
to drink water (stem inferred from the Ming 飮; usu is water) [飮]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan mün Balžuna usulan büküi-dür
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, just Balžuna water drinking, at the being,
sentences.i: While Chinggis Qahan was there drinking the water of the Baljuna,
sentences.n: büküi-dür is bü- 'be' + -küi + -dür, 'at the being, while': the clause hangs open and the next unit gives what happened meanwhile. mün (Ming 只) is a pointing particle, 'just, the very'. The same words close §182; the section break falls between them.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Baljuna, a lake or water (place name) [河名]
to drink water (stem inferred from the Ming 飮; usu is water) [飮]

sentences.t: Qasar eme köġü-ben Jekü, Jesüṅge, Tuqu-tan γurban köġüd(i)-jen Waṅ-Qan-dur gežü čüġen bejes nököd(i)-jer(i)-jen γarču
sentences.l: Qasar, wife, son-his-own Jekü, Jesüṅge, Tuqu-and-the-rest, three sons-his-own, to Waṅ-Qan leaving, few bare companions-with-his-own going out,
sentences.i: Qasar left his wife and his three sons, Jekü, Jesünge and Tuqu, with Wang Qan, and slipped out with only a few companions, stripped of everything,
sentences.n: Look at the reflexive-possessives: -ben in köġü-ben and -(i)jen in köġüd(i)-jen both mean 'his own', and the Ming marks them 自的. The (i) in köġüd(i), nököd(i)-jer(i)-jen is Shiratori's linking vowel. gežü (Ming 撇着, 'casting aside') is the same ge- as in gebe at the end of §184; it may be keġe- 'say' in an idiom, and I cannot settle it. -tan in Tuqu-tan, Ming 等 'and the rest', is how I read it; the suffix is not sure. bejes 'bare' (Ming 罄身) is a guess at the form.

morph.gloss: son (short form of köġün) [子自的行]
Tuqu, a man's name [人名 等]
and those with him (Ming 等 and the rest; analysis uncertain)
reflexive-possessive: one's own (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel)
Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid (Chinese wang 'prince' + qan) [人名 行]
to cast aside, leave behind (Ming 撇; possibly the 'say' verb keġe-; uncertain) [撇着]
bare, with only one's body (Ming 罄身; perhaps beje 'body' + -s; uncertain) [罄身]
companion [伴當每 領着自的行]

sentences.t: aqa-juγ̇an keġen Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-i erin Qaraγ̇un-Židun-u niruγ̇ud kigürižü olun jadan jadažu širi širbusun idežü jabuγ̇ad Balžuna-da Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur neilebe.
sentences.l: Elder-brother-his-own saying, Čiṅgis Qaγan-ACC seeking, Qaraγ̇un-Židun's ridges following, finding unable, lacking, raw hide, sinew eating, going, at Balžuna to Čiṅgis Qaγan joined.
sentences.i: Saying 'my elder brother', he went looking for Chinggis Qahan along the ridges of Qara'un-Jidun; unable to find him, and in want, eating raw hide and sinew as he went, he joined Chinggis Qahan at Baljuna.
sentences.n: Another long converb chain on one finite verb (neilebe 'joined', Ming 相合了): keġen, erin, kigürižü, olun, jadan, jadažu, idežü, jabuγ̇ad. aqa-juγ̇an is aqa 'elder brother' + the reflexive-possessive after a vowel, 'his own elder brother'; the keġen closes a quotation of one word. olun jadan is 'finding, unable', then jadažu 'in want' (Ming 不得 / 因乏着): the same jada- carries both senses. kigürižü is inferred from the Ming 緣着 'following the edge of'. The two broken-off words širi širbusun (生皮 'raw hide', 筋 'sinew') are what he ate. Qaraγ̇un-Židun: the Ming says only 'a mountain name'.

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own (after a vowel, back-vowel form)
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
a mountain name (Ming 山名) [山名 的]
ridge, spine of a range (Ming 嶺) [嶺每]
to go along, follow the edge of (stem inferred from the Ming 緣) [緣着]
to be in want, to be unable [因乏着]
raw, fresh (hide) (Ming 生皮 raw hide) [生皮]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to join, unite (stem inferred from the Ming 相合) [相合了]

sentences.t: Qasar-i ireġülüġed bajasču Čiṅgis Qaγan Waṅ-Qan-dur elčin ileje keġen ejetüžü
sentences.l: Qasar-ACC having caused to come, rejoicing, Čiṅgis Qaγan to Waṅ-Qan envoy let-us-send saying, consulting,
sentences.i: Rejoicing to have Qasar brought to him, Chinggis Qahan took counsel, saying 'Let us send an envoy to Wang Qan,'
sentences.n: The causative -ġül- in ireġülüġed (Ming 敎來了, 'made come') is why I have 'brought'; but who brought whom is not stated. ileje is ile- 'send' + -je, the first-person plural hortative ('let us send'). The sentence runs on with ejetüžü 'consulting' (Ming 商量着).

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid (Chinese wang 'prince' + qan) [人名 行]
hortative, first person plural: let us
to consult, deliberate (stem inferred from the Ming 商量) [商量着]

sentences.t: Žeġürijedei Qaliγ̇udar, Urjaṅqadai Čaγurqan qojar(i)-jar ügüležü ilerün Qān ečige-de Qasar-un üge keġen ügüledkün keġen ügülerün:
sentences.l: Žeġürijedei Qaliγ̇udar, Urjaṅqadai Čaγurqan, by the two, speaking, when sending: 'To Qan father, Qasar's word,' saying, 'say,' saying, saying:
sentences.i: He sent Qali'udar of the Je'üriyedei and Chaqurqan of the Uriangqadai, the two, with a message, and as he sent them he said: 'Say to Father Qan, "A word from Qasar", and speak thus:'
sentences.n: Two quotations nest here, and the colon at ügülerün tells you the inner one is about to begin. qojar(i)-jar is qojar 'two' + the instrumental -jar, 'by means of the two' (Ming 兩箇行敎: 'through the two'); the two names are men's names with a tribe-word, as the Ming says (種名, 人名). ügüledkün is ügüle- + the plural polite imperative -dkün, 'say (you both)'. The second keġen closes the instruction and ügülerün opens the message that follows. ilerün (Ming 去的 'going') is ile- 'send' with -rün; 'sending' is my reading.

morph.gloss: a man of the Jeürijed (Ming 種名; analysis uncertain) [種(名)]
a man of the Uriangqai (Urjaṅqai + -dai, person of; suffix uncertain) [種(名)]
instrumental: by, through (the Ming 行敎 marks the sending by them)
to send (the Ming gives 去 'go'; uncertain) [去的]
ruler, sovereign, khan (short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]

sentences.t: "Aqa-γ̇an qaražu qaraγ̇a in-ü žabqaba.
sentences.l: "Elder-brother-my-own looking, his sight vanished.
sentences.i: "I looked toward my elder brother, but he had gone from sight.
sentences.n: The speaker is now Qasar, and the reflexive -γ̇an (Ming 自的) means 'my own'; the reflexive follows the speaker, not the grammatical subject of the sentence. qaraγ̇a (Ming 形影, 'shape and shadow') I render 'sight': what the speaker could see of him. in-ü is the third-person genitive, 'his', placed after its noun. žabqa- 'vanish' is inferred from the Ming 不見了.

morph.gloss: sight, shape, figure seen (Ming 形影 form and shadow) [形影]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to vanish, be lost (stem inferred from the Ming 不見) [不見了]

sentences.t: Qaižu qaγ̇uluγa in-ü olun jadaba.
sentences.l: Treading, road his finding unable.
sentences.i: Following his track, I could not find his road.
sentences.n: Qaižu (Ming 踏着, 'treading') I cannot parse for sure: the stem is read from the Ming alone. olun jadaba is the pattern seen in the last unit but one: 'finding' + 'unable', a negative of ability, here with the finite past -ba.

morph.gloss: to tread, follow a track (stem inferred from the Ming 踏; uncertain) [踏着]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to be in want, to be unable [不能了]

sentences.t: Qailaža daγ̇u-ban ese sonosdaba.
sentences.l: Calling, voice-my-own not heard-was.
sentences.i: I called out, but my voice was not heard.
sentences.n: ese 'not' is the negative of a past action (ülü is the negative of a present or converb). sonosdaba is sonos- 'hear' + the passive -da-, Ming 被聽得了, so 'was heard'; the reading is the Ming's. The ending of Qailaža is -ža, a spelling of the converb -žu.

morph.gloss: to call out (stem inferred from the Ming 叫) [叫着]

sentences.t: Hodud qaražu urubaṅ deretü bolžu kebtemü bi.
sentences.l: Stars looking, urubaṅ pillow-having becoming, lying I.
sentences.i: Gazing at the stars, I lie with my urubaṅ for a pillow.
sentences.n: urubaṅ has no Ming gloss at all, and I do not know the word: it may be a word for the arm or for a manner of lying, and I have left it untranslated. deretü is dere 'pillow' + the possessive -tü, so 'pillow-having', and bolžu 'becoming' makes it 'taking as his pillow'. bi here is 'I' (Ming 我); in the next unit the same spelling is the verb 'is'.

morph.gloss: the Ming gives no gloss; sense unknown (perhaps a word for the arm or a manner adverb)

sentences.t: Eme köġün min-u Qān ečige-dür bi.
sentences.l: Wife, son my, Qan father-with are.
sentences.i: My wife and my son are with Father Qan.
sentences.n: bi is 'is, are' here (Ming 有); min-u 'my' is set after both nouns, which is how the Mongolian puts a shared possessor. ečige-dür is 'at the father', the dative-locative -dür, which the Ming renders 行. 'Qān ečige' is 'Father Qan': Wang Qan, as at §178.

morph.gloss: my, of me (bi, genitive stem min-, + -u, set after its noun) [我的]
ruler, sovereign, khan (short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]

sentences.t: Itegemži ereġen oluγ̇asu Qān ečige-dür odqu bi. keġežü ilebe. keġen ügüledkün"
sentences.l: Reliance seeking, if finding, to Qan father going I saying, he sent: saying, say you."
sentences.i: 'If I can find some support to lean on, I shall go to Father Qan.' This I say, and have sent; tell him so."
sentences.n: Itegemži (Ming 倚仗, 'rely on') is a noun I read as 'a support' (itege- 'rely' + -mži); ereġen is 'seeking' (ere-), with an ending I cannot name; oluγ̇asu is ol- 'find' + the conditional -uγ̇asu, 'if (I) find'. Between them the Ming says 倚仗 指望 得呵. The structure is quote-in-quote: ' … odqu bi keġežü ilebe keġen ügüledkün' is 'saying "I shall go", he sent; saying that, say it!', with ilebe (ile- 'send', Ming 去了 'went') uncertain; I follow 'sent'.

morph.gloss: one to be relied upon, a trusted one (itege- 'to rely' + -mži; Ming 倚仗; form uncertain) [倚仗]
to seek, look for (stem inferred from the Ming 指望) [指望]
ruler, sovereign, khan (short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]
to send (the Ming reads 去了 'went'; uncertain) [去了]

sentences.t: basa ügülerün: "Ba tan-i udaγ̇aran ködölžü Kelüren-ü Arγal-Kögi-de bolžalduja; ta tende iredkün" keġen
sentences.l: Again speaking: "We you-ACC straight-after, moving, Kelüren's at Arγal-Kögi let us fix a meeting; you there come," saying,
sentences.i: He spoke again: 'We shall set out right behind you; let us fix a meeting at Arqal-Kögi on the Kelüren. Come there, all of you,' he said,
sentences.n: ba is 'we' (Ming 俺, the exclusive we; the Ming uses 咱 for the inclusive bida); tan-i is ta 'you (plural polite)' with the accusative, the object of following. udaγ̇aran 'straightway' (Ming 隨卽) is read from the Ming; I do not know its ending. bolžalduja is bolža- 'fix a meeting' + the reciprocal -ldu- + the hortative -ja, 'let us'; iredkün is ire- + the plural polite imperative -dkün. The place Arγal-Kögi has only a gloss 'place name'.

morph.gloss: we (first-person plural pronoun; Ming 俺) [俺]
you, plural polite (stem tan- before a case ending) [您行]
right after, straightway (adverb; Ming 隨卽; from udaγ̇a- 'follow'; analysis uncertain) [隨卽]
to move, set out (stem inferred from the Ming 動着) [動着]
the Kelüren, a river [河名 的]
a place name (Ming 地名) [地名 行]
to appoint a meeting (stem inferred; Ming 約會) [相約着]
hortative, first person plural: let us
there, then (locative adverb from tere) [那裏]

sentences.t: bolžaldužu tedüi Qaliγ̇udar, Čaγurqan qojar-i ileġed
sentences.l: Having agreed a meeting, thereupon Qaliγ̇udar, Čaγurqan, the two ACC, having sent,
sentences.i: Having fixed the meeting, he then sent off Qali'udar and Chaqurqan, the two,
sentences.n: Compare bolžalduja (hortative, 'let us fix') with the converb bolžaldužu 'having fixed' (Ming 約會了着). ileġed 'having sent' (Ming 敎去了) is the converb of completed action. tedüi again marks the next step.

morph.gloss: to appoint a meeting [約會了着]

sentences.t: Žürčedei, Arγai qojar-i alginčilažu
sentences.l: Žürčedei, Arγai, the two ACC, acting as vanguard,
sentences.i: and with Jürchedei and Arqai, the two, set as scouts ahead,
sentences.n: alginčilažu (Ming 頭哨做着) is read as 'acting as vanguard' (algin- 'advance' + -či agent + -la- verb-maker + -žu): the stem is guessed from the Ming. qojar-i is qojar 'two' + the accusative -i: the two are what he sets going.

morph.gloss: to act as vanguard, scout ahead (algin 'advance'? + -či + -la-; Ming 頭哨做) [頭哨做着]

sentences.t: Balžuna naγ̇ur-ača Čiṅgis Qaγan udaγ̇aran eġüsülčežü γarun morilaγsaγ̇ar Kelüren-ü Arγal-Kögi-de kürbe.
sentences.l: Balžuna lake-from, Čiṅgis Qaγan straight-after, setting out together, going out, horse-riding-as-having, Kelüren's at Arγal-Kögi reached.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan himself set out from Lake Baljuna close behind them, riding out together with his men, and reached Arqal-Kögi on the Kelüren.
sentences.n: One more converb chain: eġüsülčežü 'setting out together' (Ming 共起着), γarun 'going out', morilaγsaγ̇ar 'riding' (mori 'horse' + -la-; the ending -γsaγ̇ar I read as 'as, just as having mounted', Ming 依着, but its form is a guess), then the finite kürbe 'reached'. naγ̇ur-ača is the ablative -ača, 'from the lake'.

morph.gloss: Baljuna, a lake or water (place name) [水名]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
right after, straightway (adverb; Ming 隨卽; from udaγ̇a- 'follow'; analysis uncertain) [隨卽]
to rise and set out together (stem inferred from the Ming 共起) [共起着]
to mount a horse, ride (mori 'horse' + -la-) [上馬依着]
"just as, in the manner of having -ed" (Ming 依着; analysis uncertain)
the Kelüren, a river [河名 的]
a place name (Ming 地名) [地名 行]

sentences.t: Qaliγ̇udar, Čaγurqan qojar Waṅ-Qan-dur kürčü Qasar-un üge keġen endēče ügüležü ilegsen üges ügüležüġüi.
sentences.l: Qaliγ̇udar, Čaγurqan, the two, to Waṅ-Qan arriving, Qasar's word saying, from here speaking, sent words spoke.
sentences.i: Qali'udar and Chaqurqan came to Wang Qan and spoke the words that had been sent from here: 'a word from Qasar'.
sentences.n: The sentence has two quotation closers, keġen and the participle ilegsen 'sent' (ile- + -gsen), the second turning the message into 'the words sent from here' (endēče, ene 'this' + the long-vowel ablative). ügüležüġüi 'spoke' is ügüle- + a past ending I cannot name for certain (Ming 說了有).

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid (Chinese wang 'prince' + qan) [人名 行]

sentences.t: Waṅ-Qān altan terme bosγažu gened qurimlan ažuγ̇ui.
sentences.l: Waṅ-Qān, golden tent raising, unawares, feasting, was.
sentences.i: Wang Qan had set up his golden tent and was holding a feast, unawares.
sentences.n: gened 'unawares' (Ming 不意) means the speaker's side did not expect it: Wang Qan is feasting while the envoys arrive; the form is uncertain. altan terme is 'gold tent' (terme, Ming 撒帳, 'spread tent'). bosγažu is bos- 'rise' + the causative -γa-, 'raise'. qurimlan is qurim 'feast' made into a verb, 'feasting'. ažuγ̇ui is a- 'be' + a past ending; the form is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid (Chinese wang 'prince' + qan) [人名]
tent (Ming 撒帳 spread tent) [撒帳]
suddenly, unawares (form uncertain, sense from the Ming 不意) [不意]

sentences.t: Qaliγ̇udar, Čaγurqan qojar-un üge-dür Waṅ-Qān ügülerün:
sentences.l: Qaliγ̇udar, Čaγurqan, the two's word-at, Waṅ-Qān speaking:
sentences.i: At the words of Qali'udar and Chaqurqan, Wang Qan said:
sentences.n: üge-dür is the pattern of §178: üge 'word' + dative-locative, 'at the words' (Ming 語 裏). The colon marks that his speech follows.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid (Chinese wang 'prince' + qan) [人名]

sentences.t: "Tein böġesü Qasar iretügei" keġežü itegemži Itürgen-i ileje" keġen ileldüžüġüi.
sentences.l: "Thus if-it-be, Qasar let come," saying, trusted Itürgen-ACC "let us send," saying, sent-together.
sentences.i: "If so, let Qasar come," he said, and "Let us send Itürgen, the trusted one," and had him sent along.
sentences.n: böġesü is bü- 'be' + the conditional -ġesü, 'if it be so'; iretügei is the optative -tügei, 'let him come'. itegemži (Ming 倚仗的, 'one relied upon') is a title or epithet before Itürgen's name; it is the same word as in §183, where I read it 'a support'. ileldüžüġüi has -ldü- (Ming 共 'together') and the past ending -žüġüi; I take it as 'sent along with them'.

morph.gloss: one to be relied upon, a trusted one (itege- 'to rely' + -mži; Ming 倚仗; form uncertain) [倚仗的]
Itürgen, a man's name [人名 行]
hortative, first person plural: let us

sentences.t: Tedüi ireġed bolžal γažar-a Arγal-Kögi-de kürküi-lüġe baruγ̇a jeke-ji üžežü Itürgen elčin qarin dutaγ̇ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Thereupon having come, to the appointed place Arγal-Kögi at the arriving, a great form seeing, Itürgen the envoy back fled.
sentences.i: Then they came back, and at the instant they reached the meeting place at Arqal-Kögi, Itürgen the envoy caught sight of something large and fled back.
sentences.n: kürküi-lüġe (kür- 'reach' + -küi + -lüġe 'with') means 'as soon as arriving'; the analysis of -lüġe is tentative. baruγ̇a jeke-ji (Ming 形影 大行) is 'a great shape' with the accusative -ji: I do not know what he sees. It may be Chinggis's gathered force, but the Ming gives only 'form and shadow'. qarin is 'back' (Ming 囘) as an adverb, or qari- 'return' + -n. dutaγ̇ažuγ̇u (dutaγ̇a- 'flee' + -žuγ̇u) is the finite past.

morph.gloss: a place name (Ming 地名) [地名 行]
with; after a participle, as soon as (analysis tentative)
shape, figure seen (Ming 形影 form and shadow; sense uncertain) [形影]

sentences.t: Qaliγ̇udar-un morin qurdun ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Qaliγ̇udar's horse swift was.
sentences.i: Qali'udar's horse was fast.
sentences.n: ažuγ̇u 'was' (Ming 有來) is a- 'be' + -žuγ̇u; the plain past of being. qurdun (Ming 快) leaves it open whether 'swift' is adjective or adverb.

sentences.t: Qaliγ̇udar, güjičežü bariqu žürüge jadažu uridaγ̇un qoinaγ̇un in-ü hoγtoriγan jabuqui-dur
sentences.l: Qaliγ̇udar overtaking, seizing heart unable, front, back his crosswise, at the going,
sentences.i: Qali'udar overtook him, but could not bring himself to seize him; and as the man went cutting across, before and behind him,
sentences.n: This is the hardest passage in the part. güjičežü is 'overtaking' (stem from the Ming 趕上着); bariqu žürüge jadažu (Ming 拿的 心 不能着) is 'the seizing heart unable', which I read as 'could not bring himself to seize'; but it could equally be 'could not grasp (the man) firmly'. uridaγ̇un qoinaγ̇un in-ü hoγtoriγan 'front, back, his, crosswise (Ming 横斷)' is the Ming's reading; the endings -γ̇un are not clear to me and who is moving where is not stated. I give a literal render and a smoothed one; neither is certain.

morph.gloss: to overtake, chase (stem inferred from the Ming 趕上) [趕上着]
to take hold of, seize [拿的]
to be in want, to be unable [不能着]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
crosswise, cutting across (Ming 横斷; form uncertain) [横斷]

sentences.t: Čaγurqan-u morin udaγ̇an ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Čaγurqan's horse slow was.
sentences.i: Chaqurqan's horse was slow.
sentences.n: The contrast with the last-but-one unit: Qaliγ̇udar's horse was fast (qurdun), Čaγurqan's slow (udaγ̇an, Ming 遲).

sentences.t: Qoināča sumun-u kürküi üžeġür-e Itürgen-ü altan emeġeltü qara aγta-jin γujaṅ hužaγ̇ur saγ̇utala qarbužuγ̇u.
sentences.l: From behind arrow's arriving, at the tip, Itürgen's golden saddle-having black gelding's rump tip, until sitting, shot.
sentences.i: An arrow, arriving from behind, shot Itürgen, striking the rump of his black gelding with the golden saddle, the point of it, as far as where he sat.
sentences.n: The object of qarbužuγ̇u 'shot' is not given, and the English above is my best reading; the Ming is clear only word by word. kürküi is the participle 'arriving, the arrival' (Ming 到的); üžeġür-e (Ming 捎頭 行) 'at the tip'. qoināča is qoina 'behind' + the short ablative -ča. emeġeltü is 'saddle-having'. hužaγ̇ur is 'root' elsewhere, here glossed 尖 'point, tip'. saγ̇utala is saγ̇u- 'sit' + the terminal converb -tala, 'until sitting'; I take it that the shot carried through to the rider's seat, but it is not said.

morph.gloss: arrow (the plain stem is sumu) [箭 的]
tip, end (Ming 捎頭) [捎頭 行]
end, tip; elsewhere 'root, origin' (Ming here 尖 point) [尖]
to shoot (stem inferred from the Ming 射) [射了]

sentences.t: Tende Itürgen-i Qaliγ̇udar, Čaγurqan qojar barižu Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur abčiraba.
sentences.l: There Itürgen-ACC, Qaliγ̇udar, Čaγurqan, the two, seizing, Čiṅgis to Qaγan brought.
sentences.i: There Qali'udar and Chaqurqan, the two, seized Itürgen and brought him to Chinggis Qahan.
sentences.n: A short chain: barižu 'seizing' + abčiraba 'brought' (Ming 將來了). abčira- seems to be ab- 'take' plus a second verb; the analysis is not sure. Itürgen-i and Qaliγ̇udar … qojar are the accusative object and the doubled subject.

morph.gloss: there, then (locative adverb from tere) [那裏]
Itürgen, a man's name [人名 行]
to take hold of, seize [拿着]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to bring along (ab- 'take' + a second verb; uncertain) [將來了]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Itürgen-dür ülü keleleldün Qasar-tur abču odudqun; Qasar medetügei" keġebe.
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan: to Itürgen not talk-with; to Qasar taking, go (you two); Qasar let know, said.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan said: "Do not speak with Itürgen; take him to Qasar. Qasar will know what to do."
sentences.n: Chinggis gives an order of three parts: a prohibition with ülü ('do not talk with him'), a plural imperative odudqun (od- 'go' + -dqun, 'go, you two'), and an optative medetügei (mede- 'know' + -tügei, 'let Qasar know'). keleleldün is read from the Ming 不 說話; the root and ending are not certain, and I take it as 'converse'. The print closes the quotation at medetügei with a quotation mark but puts no opening mark at the start of the order.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to talk with one another (kele- 'tongue, speak' + -le- + reciprocal -l-; analysis uncertain) [說話]

sentences.t: abču oduγ̇asu Qasar Itürgen-dür ülü keleleldün mün tende čabčižü gebe.
sentences.l: Taking, if going, Qasar, to Itürgen not talk-with, just there cutting, cast aside.
sentences.i: When they took him, Qasar did not speak with Itürgen but cut him down on the spot and left him.
sentences.n: oduγ̇asu is od- 'go' + the conditional -uγ̇asu, 'if (they) went' (Ming 去呵); I read it 'when'. čabčižü gebe: the converb 'cutting' followed by ge- (Ming 撇 'cast aside'), the same word as in §183. keleleldün appears in both Chinggis's order and Qasar's execution of it: he obeyed to the letter.

morph.gloss: to talk with one another (kele- 'tongue, speak' + -le- + reciprocal -l-; analysis uncertain) [說話]
there, then (locative adverb from tere) [那裏]
to cast aside, dispose of (Ming 撇; uncertain) [撇了]

sentences.t: Qaliγ̇udar, Čaγurqan qojar Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a ügülerün:
sentences.l: Qaliγ̇udar, Čaγurqan, the two, Čiṅgis Qaγan-to speaking:
sentences.i: Qali'udar and Chaqurqan spoke to Chinggis Qahan:
sentences.n: Qaγan-(n)a is the dative-locative -(n)a (the n in brackets is Shiratori's), and the Ming 行 gives its sense 'to'. ügülerün opens their report, which the quotation marks that follow carry.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Waṅ-Qān gened bi.
sentences.l: "Waṅ-Qān unawares is.
sentences.i: "Wang Qan is off his guard.
sentences.n: gened 'unawares' (Ming 不意) is again the key word; the next unit says what he is doing.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid (Chinese wang 'prince' + qan) [人名]
suddenly, unawares (form uncertain, sense from the Ming 不意) [不意]

sentences.t: Altan terme bosγažu qurimlamui.
sentences.l: Gold tent raising, feasting is.
sentences.i: He has set up his golden tent and is holding a feast.
sentences.n: The same two events as in §184, now told to Chinggis in the present: qurimlamui, qurim 'feast' + -la- + the present -mui.

morph.gloss: tent (Ming 撒帳 spread tent) [撒帳]

sentences.t: Ötörlen igülgüžü sünid düliligežü nemden büčije" keġebe
sentences.l: Quickly, igülgüžü, by nights riding-on-and-on, surprise, let us surround," he said.
sentences.i: Let us hurry, ride on through the nights, and surround him by surprise," he said.
sentences.n: A plan in converbs and one hortative: ötörlen 'hurrying' (Ming 作急), igülgüžü (Ming silent; stem unknown, perhaps a second word for haste or readiness), düliligežü 'riding on and on' (Ming 兼行兼行着, night and day), nemden 'by surprise' (Ming 掩襲), and büčije, büči- 'surround' + the hortative -je, 'let us surround' (Ming 圍咱). The nights are plural (sünid), and the speech ends without a mark but with keġebe.

morph.gloss: to hurry (stem inferred from the Ming 作急) [快]
the Ming gives no gloss; sense unknown (stem uncertain)
to ride on and on, press forward (Ming 兼行兼行 night and day; stem uncertain) [兼行兼行着]
by surprise, in a surprise attack (Ming 掩襲; form uncertain) [掩襲]
hortative, first person plural: let us

sentences.t: Ene üge-ji žöbšiježü Žürčedei, Arγai qojar-i alginčilaγ̇ulžu
sentences.l: This word-ACC, approving, Žürčedei, Arγai, the two ACC, causing to act as vanguard,
sentences.i: Approving this plan, he had Jürchedei and Arqai, the two, go ahead as scouts,
sentences.n: žöbšiježü (Ming 道是着) is 'agreeing, approving' (žöb 'right' + -šije- + -žü); üge-ji has the accusative -ji. alginčilaγ̇ulžu adds the causative -γ̇ul- to the verb of §183: 'made them act as vanguard'.

morph.gloss: to approve, agree to (Ming 道是) [道是着]
to act as vanguard [敎頭哨着]

sentences.t: Sünid düliġed kürčü Žežeġer- Ündür-ün Žer-Qabčiγai-jin amasar-a büküi-dür büčibe.
sentences.l: By nights having ridden day and night, arriving, Žežeġer-Ündür's Žer-Qabčiγai's at the mouth, at the being, surrounded.
sentences.i: Riding on through the nights they came to the mouth of Jer-Qabchigai in the Jeje'er Height, and surrounded him there.
sentences.n: Žežeġer- and Ündür-ün are one name split over the line, 'Jeje'er-Ündür' (the Ming calls it 'mountain name'); Žer-Qabčiγai-jin is a second name, 'Jer-Qabchigai', which I think means a narrow gorge but that is a guess; amasar-a is 'at the mouth, entrance'. büküi-dür is 'at the being, while being there'.

morph.gloss: to ride day and night (stem inferred from the Ming 兼行) [兼行了]
Jeje'er, a mountain name (the Ming says 山 'mountain'; the hyphen carries over to the next word) [山]
height, high place (a name; Ming 名的) [名的]
a place name (Ming 地名); qabčiγai perhaps 'narrow gorge' [地名 的]

sentences.t: γurban sünid γurban üdüd bulγaγdarun bučižu baibasu
sentences.l: Three nights, three days being fought, surrounding, if (they) stood,
sentences.i: For three nights and three days they were fought; surrounding him, they stood their ground,
sentences.n: bulγaγdarun is bulγa- 'fight' + the passive -γda- + the time converb -run, 'when being fought' (Ming 被厮殺時); baibasu is bai- 'stand' + the conditional -basu, Ming 立呵, 'if (they) stood'. The sentence has no finite verb until the next unit. The nights and days are plurals in -d.

sentences.t: γutuγ̇ar üdür jadažu müd oroba.
sentences.l: Third day, in want, they entered.
sentences.i: On the third day, hard pressed, they gave themselves up.
sentences.n: oroba is oro- 'enter' + -ba; the Ming 投入了 means 'came over, went in to join', i.e. surrendered. müd 'they' (Ming 他每) is a form I am not sure of. jadažu again 'in want'.

morph.gloss: to be in want, to be unable [窮乏着]

sentences.t: Waṅ-Qān, Seṅgüm qojar-i süni ker ber γaruγsan-i ese medegdebe.
sentences.l: Waṅ-Qān, Seṅgüm, the two ACC, night how even the going out ACC, not caused to know.
sentences.i: It was not known how Wang Qan and Senggum, the two, had gone out in the night.
sentences.n: γaruγsan-i is γar- 'go out' + the participle -γsan + the accusative -i; medegdebe is mede- 'know' + the passive -gde-, 'was known'. ker … ber 'how even' (Ming 怎生 也) is 'in whatever way'. ese 'not' (Ming 不曾) is the negative of the past, not ülü.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, ruler of the Kereid (Chinese wang 'prince' + qan) [人名]
to go out [出了的 行]

sentences.t: Ene bulγalduuγči Žirgin-u Qdaγ-Baγ̇atur ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: This fighter, Jirgin's Qdaγ-Baγ̇atur, was.
sentences.i: There was one fighter, Qadaq-Ba'atur of the Jirgin.
sentences.n: bulγalduuγči is bulγa- 'fight' + -ldu- + the agent -uγči, 'one who fights'. Shiratori prints Qdaγ-Baγ̇atur, with no a after the Q; this is probably a slip for Qadaγ- (as printed later in the same §), and I give the name as 'Qadaq-Ba'atur'. Žirgin-u is 'of the Jirgin', a people-name with the genitive.

morph.gloss: Qadaq-Ba'atur (Shiratori prints Qdaγ here without the a), a man's name and title 'hero' [人名 勇士]

sentences.t: Qdaγ-Baγ̇atur orožu irežü ügülerün:
sentences.l: Qdaγ-Baγ̇atur entering, coming, speaking:
sentences.i: Qadaq-Ba'atur came in to him and said:
sentences.n: orožu irežü, two converbs: 'entering, coming' (Ming 投着 來着), i.e. 'coming over'. The colon opens his speech.

morph.gloss: Qadaq-Ba'atur (Shiratori prints Qdaγ here without the a), a man's name and title 'hero' [人名 勇士]

sentences.t: "Γurban sünid γurban üdüd bulγaldurun tus qān-(n)i-jan üžeġed barižu
sentences.l: "Three nights, three days when fighting, own true lord-ACC-his seeing, seizing,
sentences.i: "Through three nights and three days of fighting I saw my own true lord and held him,
sentences.n: The morph -(n)i-jan in qān-(n)i-jan is the accusative -(n)i + the reflexive-possessive -jan: 'his own lord, as object'. The Ming glosses it 皇帝自的行 and tus qān as 正主 'rightful lord'. bulγaldurun is the same time converb as before, active this time. barižu 'seizing' (Ming 拿着): here maybe 'holding on to, taking care of'; the speech is hard from here.

morph.gloss: own, rightful (tus qān 'one's own true lord') [正主]
to take hold of, seize [拿着]

sentences.t: ker alaγ̇ulqu keġen tebčin jadažu ami-jan qoroqun küṅgetügei keġen soγ̇oraγ̇ulun bulγaldulaγ̇a bi.
sentences.l: How let kill saying, giving up unable, life-his-own holding-in-the-mouth, let be far saying, luring, fought I.
sentences.i: thinking 'How can I let him be killed?' I could not give him up; I held my life between my teeth, and, saying 'Let him be far away,' I drew them on and fought.
sentences.n: alaγ̇ulqu is ala- 'kill' + the causative -γ̇ul- + the participle -qu, 'to cause to be killed'. tebčin jadažu (Ming 棄捨 不能着): 'unable to give up'. qoroqun (Ming 刁着) 'holding in the mouth' is the Ming's gloss and its stem is not sure: I take the phrase as 'risking my life', an idiom. küṅgetügei is 'let it be far', optative -tügei; keġen closes the thought. The last verb has -laγ̇a, with bi 'I' after it.

morph.gloss: giving up, abandoning (verbal noun; form not analysed) [棄捨]
to be in want, to be unable [不能着]
to hold in the mouth, clench in the teeth (stem uncertain) [刁着]
to be far, be kept far off (stem inferred from the Ming 離的遠) [敎離的遠者︀]
to lure, draw on (stem inferred from the Ming 引鬭) [引鬭]

sentences.t: Edöġe üküġüldeġešü üküšü.
sentences.l: Now if caused to die, let me die.
sentences.i: Now, if I am to be put to death, let me die.
sentences.n: üküġüldeġešü stacks suffixes: ükü- 'die' + the causative -ġül- + the passive -de- + the conditional -ġešü, 'if made to die'. üküšü is the first-person optative -šü, 'let me die', from the Ming 死我.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a sojurγaγdaγ̇asu küčü ögsü" keġebe.
sentences.l: Čiṅgis to Qaγan if favoured, strength let me give," said.
sentences.i: But if Chinggis Qahan shows me favour, I will give him my strength," he said.
sentences.n: sojurγaγdaγ̇asu is sojurγa- 'show favour' + the passive -γda- + the conditional -γasu, 'if shown favour' (Ming 被恩賜呵). ögsü, 'let me give', is the optative of ög-. 'Give strength' (küčü ög-) is the Mongol idiom for serving.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Qadaγ-Baγ̇atur-un üge-ji žöbšiježü žarliγ bolurun
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan Qadaγ-Baγ̇atur's word-ACC approving, decree making when:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan approved Qadaq-Ba'atur's words, and when he made his decree:
sentences.n: bolurun (bol- 'become' + -urun) has the Ming 做的, 'making'; žarliγ bol- is 'make a decree'. The colon is missing from the print here, but the decree follows.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Qadaq-Ba'atur, a man's name and title 'hero' [人名勇士的]
to approve, agree to (Ming 道是) [道是着]

sentences.t: tus qān-(n)i-jan tebčin jadažu amin qoroqun küṅgetügei keġen
sentences.l: "Own true lord giving-up unable, life holding-in-the-mouth, let him be far saying,
sentences.i: "He could not give up his own true lord; holding his life between his teeth, saying 'Let him be far away,'
sentences.n: Compare the same words in Qadaq's own speech above. tus, qān, tebčin, jadažu, qoroqun, küṅgetügei, keġen are the same: Chinggis repeats them back.

morph.gloss: own, rightful (tus qān 'one's own true lord') [正主]
giving up, abandoning (verbal noun; form not analysed) [棄捨]
to be in want, to be unable [不能着]
to hold in the mouth, clench in the teeth (stem uncertain) [刁着]
to be far, be kept far off (stem inferred from the Ming 離的遠) [敎離的遠者︀]

sentences.t: bulγalduqu ere tere ülü-ü bi. Nököčegdekü küġün büleġe"
sentences.l: fighting man that, is he not? companion-to-be-made man was."
sentences.i: was he not a fighter? He was a man to make a companion of."
sentences.n: ülü-ü bi 'is it not?' (Ming 不是 有麽) is a rhetorical question: ülü 'not' + -ü, the particle of question, whose reading is uncertain (the Ming puts its 麽 on the next word, bi 'is'). Nököčegdekü is nökör 'companion' + a verb-maker + the passive -gde- + the participle -kü, 'one to be made a companion'.

sentences.t: keġeġed sojurγažu ülü üküġülün Quildar-un amin-u tula
sentences.l: Having said, favouring, not making die, Quildar's life's because of,
sentences.i: Having said this, he showed him favour and did not put him to death, for Quildar's life's sake,
sentences.n: keġeġed 'having said' closes the speech; sojurγažu 'favouring' (Ming 恩賜着) and üküġülün 'making die' (ükü- + causative, Ming 敎死) carry on. Quildar-un amin-u tula is the genitive pair + the postposition tula 'because of' (Ming 上頭, 'on top of'); why Quildar is named is not said; the next unit gives his wife and son.

morph.gloss: because of, on account of (postposition) [上頭]

sentences.t: Qadaγ-Baγ̇atur-i žaγ̇un Žirgin-i Quildar-un eme köġün-e in-ü küčü ögtügei.
sentences.l: Qadaγ-Baγ̇atur-ACC, hundred Jirgin-ACC, Quildar's wife, to son, his strength let be given.
sentences.i: Qadaq-Ba'atur and the hundred Jirgin, the decree said, were to give their strength to Quildar's wife and son.
sentences.n: The two objects (Qadaγ-Baγ̇atur-i, žaγ̇un Žirgin-i) have the accusative -i; köġün-e has the dative; ögtügei is ög- 'give' + the optative -tügei. 'His strength' (in-ü küčü) is the service of the whole group. I am reading the Ming 與者 as passive, 'let it be given', with the objects as those who give; the sentence is hard.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
optative, third person: let it be given

sentences.t: Nuγ̇un köġün töreġešü Quildar-un uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele daγažu küčü ögtügei:
sentences.l: Boy, son, if born, Quildar's lineage's lineage-to until, following, strength let be given:
sentences.i: 'If a son is born, let his strength be given from Quildar's line to the line after it, down through the generations:'
sentences.n: töreġešü is töre- 'be born' + the conditional -ġešü. uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele is the idiom 'down to the offspring of the offspring' (Ming 子孫的 子孫行 直到); the genitive and dative of the same word make the chain. daγažu 'following' (Ming 隨着) then küčü ögtügei repeats the earlier clause.

morph.gloss: Quildar, a man's name [人名 的]
optative, third person: let it be given

sentences.t: ökin köġün töreġešü ečige eke an-u öġer-ün dura-γ̇ar bu qudalatuγai:
sentences.l: Girl, son, if born, father, mother their own will-by not let betroth:
sentences.i: 'If a daughter is born, let her father and mother not betroth her by their own will:'
sentences.n: ökin köġün is 'girl-child' and köġün is 'child, son', as the Ming 女孩兒 shows. dura-γ̇ar is dura 'will' + the instrumental -γ̇ar, 'by their own will'. bu is the prohibitive, 'do not'; qudalatuγai is the Ming's 聘, 'betroth', with the optative -tuγai: the stem is guessed.

morph.gloss: their (third-person genitive, back-vowel companion of in-ü, set after its noun) [他的]
to betroth, arrange a marriage for (stem inferred from the Ming 聘) [聘者︀]

sentences.t: Quildar-un eme köġün-ü emüne ümere-ġen žarutuγai keġen sojurγan žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Quildar's wife, son's front, behind-their-own let employ," saying, favour decree became.
sentences.i: 'Let them be used at the front and rear of Quildar's wife and son.' So he said, and it became a decree of favour.
sentences.n: The two reflexive-possessives: ümere-ġen 'behind, his own' (Ming 後自的行). The phrase emüne ümere-ġen 'front and behind' I read as 'before and after themselves': the Jirgin serve them as attendants. žarutuγai is žaru- 'employ' + -tuγai (Ming 使喚者). sojurγan žarliγ bolba is 'became a decree of favour' (Ming 恩賜聖旨做了).

morph.gloss: to employ, use as a servant (stem inferred from the Ming 使喚) [使喚者︀]

sentences.t: Quildar-Sečen-ü aman urida negegsen-ü tula Čiṅgis Qaγan sojurγažu žarliγ bolurun
sentences.l: Quildar-Sečen's mouth first opened because of, Čiṅgis Qaγan favouring, decree making when:
sentences.i: Because Quildar-Sechen had opened his mouth first, Chinggis Qahan showed favour, and when he made his decree:
sentences.n: aman urida negegsen-ü tula is 'because of the one who first opened his mouth': aman 'mouth', urida 'first', negegsen the participle in -gsen with the genitive -ü, and tula 'because of' (Ming 上頭). So the favour was a reward for speaking up first; the Ming has nothing more. Name: Quildar-Sečen, Sečen being 'wise'.

morph.gloss: because of, on account of (postposition) [上頭]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Quildar-un uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele Quildar-un tusa-jin tula önečid-ün abliγa abun atuγai" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: "Quildar's lineage's lineage-to until, Quildar's favour's because of, orphans' abliγa taking let remain," saying, decree became.
sentences.i: 'Down to the line of Quildar's line, because of Quildar's favour, let them remain in receipt of the orphans' share,' he said, and it became a decree.
sentences.n: tusa-jin tula is 'because of the favour (tusa) of Quildar'. önečid-ün is 'of the orphans' (Ming 孤兒每 的). abliγa (Ming 請受, 'request and receive') I cannot place exactly: I read it as a share or grant that orphans receive; abun atuγai is 'let them remain taking' (ab- + converb -un; a- + the optative -tuγai). The sense of the whole is uncertain: it may be an exemption or a ration.

morph.gloss: because of, on account of (postposition) [上頭]
orphan (Ming 孤兒) [孤兒每 的]
a share or grant received (Ming 請受 request and receive; sense uncertain) [請受]
